title: Find out why a walk passes on its own and fails in a batch
goal: Some scripted walks pass when run one at a time but fail when several are run one after another, saying a menu they need is not on screen. That makes a batch run report failures that are not real, so a person reading it cannot tell a broken feature from a leftover from the walk before.
notes:
REPRODUCED on 2026-09-12, twice, on the working tree for the button-hug task.

  $ Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build style styled starter
  ...
  text-style-walk    16s  FAILED  step 58 (panelMenu): no menu called "Size" is in the window; the ones that are: 100% 58.0pt wide at x 869.0 says "Choose a zoom level..."
  ==> 14 passed, 1 failed

The first run of the same 15-walk batch failed BOTH text-style-walk (step 58) and text-style-arming-walk (step 73) with the identical message; the second run failed only text-style-walk, so it is not fully deterministic.

Each of those walks passes on its own:
  $ Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/text-style-walk.json          -> status ok
  $ Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/text-style-arming-walk.json --no-build -> status ok
  $ Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build styles text-style               -> 6 passed, 0 failed

Not caused by the button-hug change: text-style-walk inserts no components at all (grep for Button/component finds nothing but a Position & Size section press), and it passes on a clean tree too. Most likely the probe bundle keeps panel state (scroll position, or which section is open) in its own settings between launches, and a walk earlier in the batch leaves the Text section out of reach. text-style-walk has no setup.forget block, unlike style-on-a-copy-walk which forgets text, panel, shapes, color and tools. Starting point: the setup/forget handling in Sources/PhotonzCore/PlaytestScript.swift and whatever writes panel state on quit.
acceptance: Running Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build style styled starter twice in a row gives the same answer both times, with no walk failing that passes on its own
The cause is written down in docs/design/playtest-harness.md, whether it is state the probe keeps between launches or something the walks leave behind
A walk starts from the same state whether it is first in a batch or last
